findings.description: STK-SUP-003 requires detection when a task is skipped. SYS-SUP-005 assigns a checkpoint to the cycle in which its task was released. If a scheduled release never occurs, this assignment gives the cycle no checkpoint for that task. The missing-checkpoint rule then leaves open whether to declare a flow fault at that cycle end.
findings.requested_change: Define the expected checkpoint set independently of observed releases and specify the end-of-cycle verdict when a scheduled release never occurs. Verify that case separately from a release whose checkpoint fails to arrive.

findings.description: A configuration block can present both a failed CRC and an out-of-range value under CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-115. SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for the integrity fault and SYS-RST-003 requires a latch for the range fault. OP-SYS-040 records the unresolved validity and precedence of the two checks.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to the startup checks, fault reports, history and recovery behavior when both conditions are observable.

findings.description: After the CON-SUP-110 latch survives a reset and startup checks pass, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 hold the signals low. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-005 through SYS-MEM-008 still lack a common rule for which application and supervision functions run in that mode.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved retained-latch mode rule to application releases, supervision, runtime integrity checking, diagnostics and watchdog service.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 counts supervisor resets with the same fault code. SYS-RST-001 starts the reset deadline from the first operational fault, and SYS-RST-013 orders the report of the fault that causes the reset. When two distinct codes are reported before one reset, the set leaves the code attributed to that reset undefined, so the next startup can produce different latch counts.
findings.requested_change: Record and resolve which fault code is attributed to a supervisor reset when multiple faults precede it. Apply the rule to the reset sequence and verify a mixed-code case.

findings.description: The startup message, fault reports and service replies share the CON-SUP-007 serial line. As OP-SYS-042 shows, a GET FAULTS response can occupy the line for longer than the CON-SUP-112 fault-report budget. The set still leaves frame handling, admitted simultaneous reports and service deadline precedence undecided.
findings.requested_change: Apply the agreed traffic and frame-handling rules, then check the admitted frame lengths and concurrent traffic against both diagnostic deadlines.

findings.description: The producer of the CON-SUP-107 block and the checker in SYS-MEM-002 can use identical CRC parameters and still disagree if they serialize fields differently or include different bytes. OP-SYS-005 now records these interface decisions, and the contract remains undefined.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved serialized block layout, covered bytes and treatment of the stored CRC field. Supply reference blocks for independent verification.

findings.description: SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 direct readers to SYS-SAFE-003 for the latched hold under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115. SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 own those holds. SYS-RST-012 points to SYS-RST-002 for report completion before a reset request, which SYS-RST-013 owns. SYS-RST-013 also points to SYS-WDG-005 for window-watchdog refresh cessation, now owned by SYS-WDG-007.
findings.requested_change: Update the rationales to cite the requirements that own the current hold, report ordering and window-watchdog cessation rules.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-006 now accepts a refresh at exactly 12 ms, resolving the boundary verdict. For a missing refresh, its W2 test delegates the latest reset time to an upper limit chosen in design. The rationale of SYS-WDG-007 still says the reset occurs at exactly 12 ms. These give different timing criteria for the same CON-SUP-106 timeout.
findings.requested_change: Define a common timeout and latest reset criterion for the no-refresh case while preserving acceptance of a refresh at exactly 12 ms. Use the same criterion in the watchdog rationales and W2. Record an open point if timing tolerance needs approval.

findings.description: OP-SYS-009 says a service request received after safe-state entry cannot be answered within 50 ms when a software reset follows within 20 ms. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 give maximum intervals. A short reply can fit before some allowed reset times, and a longer reply or one received nearer the reset may be interrupted.
findings.requested_change: Assess the available service time against the actual reset sequence and permitted reply lengths. Use that assessment to frame the pending decision on accepted requests and their outcomes.

findings.description: OP-SYS-043 identifies evidence methods for CON-SUP-110 retention. The target and Renode reset behavior, startup handling of retained state, and validity of latch, history and reset-sequence records after an interrupted update still lack evidence or an agreed recovery rule.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the identified platform and simulator evidence and apply an approved interrupted-update recovery rule to the retained state requirements.

findings.description: OP-SYS-038 is marked nonblocking even though SYS-TEST-015 says its undecided stimulus can prevent any valid alive positive-control run under CON-SUP-116. SYS-TEST-001 and SYS-WDG-006 also remain proposed despite depending on the blocking message-format and first-refresh decisions in OP-SYS-002 and OP-SYS-010.
findings.requested_change: Align blocking flags and affected-item statuses with the decisions that can prevent a required demonstration or change a required outcome. Identify which remaining observation choices can be deferred.

findings.description: The reworked test rejects a run masked by an earlier timing or flow fault. It still identifies no admitted CON-SUP-116 stimulus that can suppress T_IN completion for two periods without a competing fault under SYS-SUP-003 or SYS-SUP-005. Reporting all such runs as not run leaves SYS-TEST-006 without its stated positive control.
findings.requested_change: Establish a feasible non-masking stimulus or an approved alternative that isolates alive supervision, and carry that approach into the positive-control criteria.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-011 now has finite failure criteria for missing release and missing start. If OP-SYS-013 selects task processor time under CON-SUP-103, a task that starts and is then indefinitely preempted never reaches execution-limit expiry. The completion criterion gives that nominal run no finite verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define a finite demonstration outcome for a started task that never completes or reaches execution-limit expiry. Keep that outcome consistent with the approved execution-time basis and the alive rule.

findings.description: The independent-watchdog refresh obligation holds whenever no listed task fault has become detectable since reset. That includes startup and retained-latch operation, where CON-SUP-106 gives no service or first-interval policy.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved watchdog service modes and the event anchoring the first refresh interval.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-005 and SYS-WDG-007 stop both watchdog services at the same task-fault cutoff. A watchdog already near its CON-SUP-106 expiry can reset the controller ahead of the report and software reset required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to the independent-watchdog cessation rule and its interaction with the window watchdog, reporting and software reset.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset undefined. The rationale describes fault-free operation after successful startup, and the normative text gives no event that starts the 60 s interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the intervening events that break the sequence and the approved start event for the 60 s interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the reset cause. The framing and encoding remain open, so a verifier cannot identify the message or decode the classified cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved startup-message format and the expected encoding for each reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the latest reset cause. CON-SUP-113 defines no cause field in either supported response and specifies ERR for other requests. The interaction that satisfies both decisions remains open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved service-tool interaction for retrieving the cause and reconcile it with the CON-SUP-113 protocol.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-112 phrase 'within 10 ms' leaves the observable endpoint open. The rationale selects completion of the line feed while OP-SYS-007 still treats start versus completion of transmission as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved observable endpoint in both the requirement and its verification.

findings.description: The item requires a CON-SUP-112 report for each detected fault. SYS-WDG-007 and SYS-WDG-006 can reset the controller before the report starts or completes. The item gives no approved report outcome when that reset preempts transmission.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved watchdog precedence and specify the required report outcome for reset before or during transmission.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to a watchdog reset and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity field. The task names, CODE and CONFIG listed in CON-SUP-112 give no value for that code.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity field for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: The entity for a flow fault is the affected supervised task. One CON-SUP-104 evaluation can find several missing or out-of-order checkpoints. The set gives no rule for selecting the task name required by CON-SUP-112 in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify which task name is reported for each approved single- and multiple-checkpoint fault case.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 says milliseconds since start without defining the reference event. SYS-DIAG-005 selects the latest reset and says 'the controller started' without an observable event. OP-SYS-007 leaves that origin undecided.
findings.requested_change: Define the timestamp origin using the approved observable event and apply it consistently after the relevant reset classes.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template. The request boundary, allowed state values and fault-count meaning remain open, so a verifier cannot form an agreed complete request and predict its response for a known state and fault history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved request framing, state encoding and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The 50 ms limit in CON-SUP-113 gives no agreed measurement events for receipt or transmission. A reply that starts inside 50 ms and finishes later has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved observable request and response events for timing GET STATUS.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 GET FAULTS response has no agreed wire order or completion framing. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight reports, including an empty history, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved report order, framing and completion indication for zero through eight reports.

findings.description: The 50 ms limit in CON-SUP-113 gives no agreed start event or endpoint for a multi-record reply. A transmission can begin inside the limit and finish outside it.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved timing events for GET FAULTS, including responses with zero or multiple records.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger has no mode qualification. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt an accepted request, and the set leaves request acceptance and response behavior in the latched safe state open.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved acceptance and response behavior during pending reset and retained-latch operation, including reset during an accepted response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. The recognition boundary and finite response observation window remain open, so a test cannot determine when it sent a complete unrecognized request or when a missing ERR fails.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved framing for recognizing an unrecognized request and the observable deadline for its ERR response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 measures processor use at the configured core clock. The item gives neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration that supplies it, leaving the measurement conditions unreproducible.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved core-clock setting or controlled simulator configuration.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task. CON-SUP-101 names the default tasks, and the approved set of supported identifiers remains undefined. A verifier cannot determine the verdict for an identifier outside the default configuration.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported identifier set and use it to select known and unknown values for verification.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it. The integrity criterion and reference needed to establish an independent expected verdict for a test image remain open.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and reference information used to determine the expected result for each image.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initialization, reflection and final XOR settings can give different values for the same covered bytes while using that polynomial.
findings.requested_change: Reference the complete approved CRC-32 parameters and identify an independently reproducible check value.

findings.description: Under CON-SUP-106, withholding the refresh after a flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle can leave about 2 ms before window-watchdog expiry. The resulting hardware reset can preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and keep that incident out of the supervisor-reset latch count.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved reset outcome, timing and latch-count treatment when hardware expiry competes with the software reset request.

findings.description: If a watchdog is active during the CON-SUP-107 startup checks, the time left after a failing computation may be insufficient for the CON-SUP-110 report and reset sequence. The startup watchdog policy and timing evidence remain open.
findings.requested_change: Establish the approved startup watchdog policy and the time available for reporting and requesting reset after the failing computation.

findings.description: The item orders completion of the terminating line feed before a software reset request. If the CON-SUP-106 window watchdog resets first, the ordering condition need never be exercised even though the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report is interrupted.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved report outcome when a hardware reset preempts the intended software reset request.

findings.description: The test must establish both outputs low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 give no evidence that the simulator represents external output levels during reset assertion and before software configures the pins.
findings.requested_change: Use approved evidence that covers both external outputs through reset and software takeover for every applicable reset path.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including a reset taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The stated test lacks evidence of the pin level during reset assertion and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Establish how to verify the external status level through reset assertion and software takeover for every applicable reset path.

findings.description: The startup fault test checks that neither output is high at any recorded sample. CON-SUP-109 and SYS-SAFE-007 require the uninterrupted low interval from reset. A trace that begins after software starts can miss the reset interval and early output transitions.
findings.requested_change: Combine the injected-fault test with evidence that covers both outputs throughout reset and every interval the simulator trace cannot observe.

findings.description: The sampled status trace can show low at startup fault detection while missing a high level during the preceding reset or before the first sample. CON-SUP-109 and SYS-SAFE-008 require the full low interval.
findings.requested_change: Cover reset assertion and the pre-software interval in addition to the sampled startup-fault interval.

findings.description: The rationale assumes a control cycle that starts before startup checks pass cannot contain a scheduled release after the checks pass. CON-SUP-107 bars early release, and CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave that cycle alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Define the first counted period and latest initial alive detection point for each task using the approved startup and release alignment.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 execution limit while exceeding that limit in elapsed time. The no-overrun verdict depends on the measurement basis still open in OP-SYS-013.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved execution-time basis and verify the boundary with a preempted execution.

findings.description: The timeout uses the previous refresh as its reference. If the watchdog is active and its first refresh never occurs, the item gives no expiry reference for the CON-SUP-106 fallback reset required by STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define the activation event and the expiry interval that apply before the first accepted refresh.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-006 requires all reports in history from detection while fewer than eight faults have occurred. SYS-DIAG-010 allows entry as late as the first transmitted bit. A GET FAULTS query or reset between detection and entry yields incompatible expected histories under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Use one approved history-membership event and define query results and retained content on both sides of it.

findings.description: The planned test sets reset flags and checks that the classification follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names five classes and provides no mapping or precedence for combined flags or flags retained from an earlier reset.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved classification rule and give expected classes for single, combined and retained flag patterns.

findings.description: The text requires declaration at the exact execution-limit expiry. Its rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and its verification uses a tolerance awaiting approval. The measurement resolution in CON-SUP-103 supplies no declaration tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved declaration latency from expiry in both the normative requirement and its verification.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 declares an overrun when execution is incomplete at expiry. SYS-SUP-007 forbids it for a completion measured at or below the limit. A completion just after expiry can satisfy both conditions if the CON-SUP-103 measurement maps it to the limit.
findings.requested_change: Use a consistent approved basis for expiry and the no-overrun rule. Verify completion at expiry and just after expiry with a measured value at the limit.

findings.description: With truncation, a task starting 2.05 ms after release can measure 2.0 ms and satisfy the no-fault rule. CON-SUP-103 classifies a start later than its configured limit as late. OP-SYS-027 leaves that boundary mapping unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved mapping of actual start times to the measured boundary and verify a start immediately beyond the limit.

findings.description: The demonstration checks for the SYS-RST-009 startup message. With the CON-SUP-111 message identity unresolved, the serial capture cannot distinguish it from a startup fault report or other output.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved startup-message identity and encoding to define what the capture must contain.

findings.description: When faults with the same detection instant straddle the eight-report cutoff, either tied report can be displaced. CON-SUP-113 fixes the count and leaves the tie unresolved, which changes the result returned by GET FAULTS.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved ordering of equally timed reports and verify which report is retained at the cutoff.

findings.description: From the eighth detection onward, SYS-DIAG-011 changes required membership at detection. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry by the first transmitted bit. A query or reset before entry leaves both the new report and the displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved history-membership event and define the retained set before entry, after entry and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: The ordering applies when the failing startup check causes a software reset request. A watchdog active during startup can reset after the failing computation and before either reporting or the request. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 give no timing basis that excludes this sequence.
findings.requested_change: Resolve startup watchdog operation and define how the report sequence is handled if watchdog expiry intervenes.

findings.description: The continuous latched hold under CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 provides no pin or board evidence that both outputs remain driven low, and simulator samples cannot establish those intervals without model evidence.
findings.requested_change: Establish pin and board behavior for the applicable reset paths and use evidence covering the full hold interval.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans every intervening reset. CON-SUP-003 gives no external status-pin behavior during reset or before GPIO setup. A simulator trace showing no high sample cannot establish continuous low status across those intervals.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level stays low across reset and verify the complete hold interval.

findings.description: The only entry deadline is the first transmitted bit. If a watchdog reset prevents transmission from starting, that deadline never occurs. CON-SUP-110 requires retention across watchdog reset and OP-SYS-015 leaves the outcome for the detected fault open.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether a report must appear in history when reset prevents transmission from starting and verify that case.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before report transmission. Under SYS-WDG-007 and CON-SUP-106, expiry can reset the controller before either event. The item gives no required outcome for that preemption.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence and define the safe-state and report verdict when a hardware reset occurs first.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 place evaluation and the flow fault event at cycle end. SYS-SUP-005 leaves receipt coincident with that boundary to OP-SYS-036, so the same trace can yield an arrived checkpoint or a missing-checkpoint fault.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved receipt-versus-evaluation precedence to the normative rule and the coincident-receipt test.

findings.description: The 11 s high-status interval remains a normative demonstration target starting at the status edge. CON-SUP-108 supplies 11 s for a runtime integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 supply no demonstration duration.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved demonstration duration and timing origin to this item and its dependent demonstrations.

findings.description: The reworked CON-SUP-107 code-integrity demonstration isolates its stimulus and requires a complete code 5 line. If the check never finishes and no reset or report occurs, the fallback observation limit still depends on an undefined maximum startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Give the no-reset, no-report case a finite observation limit tied to the approved startup timing.

findings.description: The reworked CON-SUP-107 configuration-integrity demonstration isolates its stimulus and requires a complete code 6 line. If the CRC check never finishes and no reset or report occurs, the fallback observation limit still depends on an undefined maximum startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Give the no-reset, no-report case a finite observation limit tied to the approved startup timing.

findings.description: The reworked CON-SUP-115 range-fault stimulus preserves the CRC. The test ends relative to the fault's detectability instant or an undefined startup limit. If an implementation never performs the range check or reports code 9, the test still has no finite failure point.
findings.requested_change: Define a finite observation bound that applies even if the range-check event and report never occur.

findings.description: The 1099-cycle minimum still assumes the first cycle begins within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-109 specify the cycle and the signal without bounding the interval between them. Marking the count as a proposal leaves its acceptance verdict unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Derive the minimum from approved alignment and duration, or anchor the observation interval to a recorded cycle boundary and derive the count from that interval.

findings.description: The reworked demonstration associates refreshes with eligible cycles and checks spacing. It still accepts a refresh anywhere after flow-check completion and before the next cycle end. A fixed 9 ms delay on every 10 ms cycle can pass those checks without establishing CON-SUP-106 cycle-end service.
findings.requested_change: Define an acceptance criterion for the time from cycle end to its associated refresh, and record the needed decision if the allowed delay is unspecified.

findings.description: The unsupported line-feed requirement is removed. The revised criterion still accepts at least one character from each field without establishing that the CON-SUP-113 STS response is complete. A reset or truncation after the first character of a longer fault-count field can pass.
findings.requested_change: Require a complete response in the demonstration and reference the approved SYS-DIAG-007 field and framing rules for identifying it.

findings.description: The item selects the end of the request as the 50 ms origin and leaves the response endpoint open. OP-SYS-007 records both CON-SUP-113 timing references as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved request and response measurement events to the demonstration.

findings.description: The watchdog cutoff is physical start-limit expiry for a late release. SYS-SUP-002 classifies the release at measured crossing under CON-SUP-103. If a refresh falls between the two, its eligibility can depend on whether the task subsequently starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Use an approved late-start mapping and define a cutoff that can be evaluated at the refresh instant. Apply it consistently to both watchdogs.

findings.description: V1 now measures refresh order and 6–12 ms spacing. It still permits any steady delay between cycle end and the next cycle end. SYS-WDG-008 limits the change in delay across cycles, so it also accepts a steady 9 ms delay and supplies no verdict for the CON-SUP-106 cycle-end obligation.
findings.requested_change: Add an independently checkable cycle-end-to-refresh criterion to V1. Base it on the approved meaning of cycle-end service and retain the separate inter-refresh check.

findings.description: The inclusive refresh prohibition can trigger a CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset before the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset request. That hardware reset can interrupt the report and does not contribute to the same-code supervisor-reset latch sequence.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence for watchdog expiry, reporting and software reset, including its effect on the latch sequence.
